correct_completion: she will have worked here for ten years.
full_sentence: By next summer, she will have worked here for ten years.
acceptable_variants: she will have been working here for ten years.
she will have spent ten years in this job.

options.text: she has worked here for ten years.
options.why_wrong: The present perfect describes a period up to now, not a period completed by a future point such as 'next summer'.

options.text: she will have worked here for ten years.
she will work here for ten years.
options.why_wrong: The simple future describes a future action, not a duration that is already completed by a future point.

options.text: she worked here for ten years last summer.
options.why_wrong: The past simple refers to a finished past period, so it cannot describe completion by a future time.

grammar_focus: Future perfect with a 'by' + future time expression
explanation: The phrase 'by next summer' sets a future deadline. The future perfect in the main clause shows that the ten-year period will be complete at that deadline. Ukrainian speakers often choose a simple future here because Ukrainian uses perfective future forms for completion, so the English perfect structure needs deliberate practice.
translation: До наступного літа вона пропрацює тут уже десять років.
